manuscriptMap.heading: Abstract
manuscriptMap.statedAim: Test whether a four-week mindfulness app improves student wellbeing.
hypotheses: The app group reports higher wellbeing than controls at week four.
manuscriptMap.designSampleStatement: Randomised controlled trial of 180 undergraduate students.
headlineResults: The programme raised wellbeing by 0.42 standard deviations relative to control.
manuscriptMap.claimedContribution: First randomised test of this brief app in a student sample.

manuscriptMap.heading: Results
headlineResults: Mean wellbeing in the programme group was 8.40 on the 1 to 7 WEMWBS short scale.
The between-group difference was statistically significant at p = .03.

figureTableInventory.caption: Descriptive statistics by condition at week four.

ambiguityFindings.description: A reported mean of 8.40 exceeds the stated 1 to 7 scale ceiling, so the scale or the statistic is misreported.

findings.claim: The Results section reports a programme-group mean of 8.40 on a scale whose stated ceiling is 7.
findings.failureScenario: A mean above the scale ceiling means the descriptive statistics cannot be trusted as reported.
findings.leanestFix: Recompute the descriptive statistics from the raw responses and reconcile the reported scale range.

confidenceRaisers: The raw pages for the Results tables and the declarations section to confirm nothing was lost in extraction.
